newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 23.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on April 23. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Indonesian President Suharto has decided to hold special ministerial meetings every three months to discuss programmes to eradicate poverty.

Trade and Industry Minister Tungky Ariwibowo has said he is optimistic Indonesia's national car programme will be completed by the time the World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules on Japan's complaint in 1999. The national car programme launched in early 1996 grants tax and duty exemptions to PT Timor Putra, controlled by President Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra, to manufacture sedans. Japan, the European Union and the United States have filed separate complaints with the WTO over the policy which they say is discriminatory and violates WTO rules.

A district court has sentenced two youth activists to six and four years in jail respectively for subversion. The activists, Dita Indah Sari and Coen Husein Pontoh, have been accused of organising a workers' strike in Surabaya, Indonesia's second city, last year, involving about 10,000 workers.

A $460 million in-orbit satellite life insurance policy has been handed over by PT Asuransi Astra Buana, which represents a consortium of national insurance companies, to the PT Satelit Palapa Indonesia (Satelindo) telecommunication company, which owns the Palapa C1 and Palapa C2 satellites.
